subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, including existing omitted persisted jobs, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: The linked bug, this PR, and the open strict-validation PR encode conflicting cron lifecycle contracts that affect existing scheduled jobs and session-state retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a persisted-row load, migration, or doctor path for existing omitted jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only rejection
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation direction after documenting user recovery for recurring jobs.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept that only newly created jobs change, but should state that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a persisted-row load, migration, or doctor path for existing omitted jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron default semantics, SQLite store migration behavior, and upgrade compatibility where recent history points most strongly to steipete.
